title: JAXA changes Hayabusa2's asteroid target due to engine malfunction
excerpt: The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency has changed the target asteroid for its Hayabusa2 space probe due to an engine malfunction, according to documents submitted to a Cabinet committee on Monday.
content:
TOKYO - The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency has changed the target asteroid for its Hayabusa2 space probe due to an engine malfunction, according to documents submitted to a Cabinet committee on Monday.

JAXA abandoned its original plan for Hayabusa2 to explore near-Earth asteroid 1998KY26 in 2031 and now aims to reach another near-Earth asteroid, 2015BM510, in fiscal 2028, the documents showed.

According to JAXA, a malfunction occurred in mid-August in one of the four ion engines, the only one being used for navigation at the time.

Although operations have continued using the remaining functional systems, the spacecraft can no longer achieve the acceleration needed to carry out a planned swing-by maneuver, in which it would use Earth's gravity to alter its trajectory.

The new target is estimated to have a diameter of 17 to 74 meters, and Hayabusa2 will observe it during a close flyby.

Hayabusa2 was launched in 2014. After returning sand samples from the asteroid Ryugu to Earth, it conducted observations while passing very close to asteroid Torifune in July this year and had been aiming to reach 1998KY26 in 2031.
